Core Principle

    
The log is the memory. No log, no sending.

    
Every send gets checked against the sent log first and written into it after. That one habit is what keeps a helpful system from ever becoming a double-message machine.

  


  

  
  

    
Start Here

    
Four things. That is everything you need to build your system and run it.

    

      
1
One paid offer with a live link — one product, one price, one link. The system runs one offer at a time; a second offer gets its own kit and its own log.

      
2
The setup prompt above — one tap on Copy the Setup Prompt, then fill in the form at the top of it. That filled form is the whole configuration.

      
3
Your handles, written down — Instagram, Facebook Page, Facebook profile, TikTok — and a note of where you are already signed in. Handles only. Never a password, anywhere, ever.

      
4
A sent log — a simple doc or table that starts empty. The prompt builds the format for you in Level 3; one row goes in for every send, forever.

Quick Tips — What Is a Connector?

    
Sixty seconds of plain talk before you touch a single setting. Read this first and everything after it will make sense.

    

      
In Plain Words

      
A connector is the bridge between Muse and an app. Connecting an app means you sign in once and give Muse permission to work inside that app for you — read the comments, check the inbox, send what you approved.

      
Why it matters: without the connector, Muse cannot see the app at all. It cannot read one comment, check one inbox, or send one message there. The automation only works on apps that are connected. No connection means the automation is talking to a wall.

    

    

      
✓
Connect only what your automation uses. If the system never touches an app, that app does not need connecting. Keep the list short and purposeful.

      
✓
You sign in once. After that, Muse works through that connection. You never hand your password to the automation — the sign-in is the permission.

      
✓
If an automation suddenly stops working, check the connector first. Apps sometimes disconnect or ask you to sign in again. Nine times out of ten, that is the whole problem.

      
✓
You stay in control. You can disconnect any app, any time, in the same place you connected it: Settings → Connectors.

      
✓
A connected app is not the same as a browser app. TikTok and YouTube have no connector at all — those run through the cloud browser prompt in the next section instead.

    

  


  
  

    
Connect First — Before You Set Up Anything

    
This comes before the form, before the kit, before the first scan. Skip it and nothing else on this page can work.

    

      
Glam's Tip — Read This First

      
The automation can only touch what Muse is connected to. So before you set up any trigger-word automation, go connect your connectors — the plugins — in Muse first, and check that every one of them shows connected. If an app is not connected, the automation cannot see it and cannot act on it. That is the number one reason a setup “does nothing.”

    

    

      
1
Open Muse and open the menu (or go straight to Settings).

      
2
Go to Settings, then Connectors.

      
3
Find the app you need — they are grouped (for example, under Social) — and tap it.

      
4
Tap Connect and follow the sign-in. It may open the app or its website — sign in and approve there.

      
5
Come back to Muse and confirm the app now shows as connected. Do not skip the confirming — “I tapped Connect” is not the same as connected.

      
6
Repeat for every app your automation touches — for example Gmail, Facebook, Instagram, Threads — all of them, before you run the automation setup.

⚠ Some apps have NO connector.

      
TikTok and YouTube — and some others — do not have a Muse connector at all. You will not find them in the Connectors list, and there is nothing to connect in Settings.

      
For those apps, you do not connect anything. Instead, Muse works through its cloud browser, and you give it a prompt that tells it to connect and work that way. No connector in the list does not mean the app cannot be worked — it means browser route, with the prompt below.

Follow Along

Why This Matters

          
“Here is the difference between a helpful system and a spammy one: memory. Before anything sends, the log gets checked. After anything sends, the log gets written. The log is the whole conscience of this machine.”

        

        

          
Follow Along

          
Learn the three-way sort — every match lands in exactly one pile:

          
    
            
  1. ORIGINAL — this person has never been messaged about this offer. They get the full original DM. It happens once.
    2. 
            
  2. NUDGE — this person was messaged before, but they commented on a new post. They get one short nudge, not the whole pitch again.
    3. 
            
  3. SKIP — same person, same post. Nothing sends. Nobody gets double-messaged, no matter how many times they comment.
    4. 
          

          
Show the log format — one row per send, kept per platform, per offer:

Codes follow the same law. If a DM ever carries a one-use code, the log records which code went to whom. A code that is not in the log was never sent — and a code already in the log never goes out twice.

Why This Matters

          
“Automation that sounds like a robot undoes the trust your content built. So your system only ever sends three messages — and all three sound like a person who likes people. You write them once, in your voice, and they never improvise.”

        

        

          
Follow Along

          
Here are the three messages exactly as the live system sends them for the PROMPT offer — use them as the model for your own:

          
1 · Public reply — posted under their comment
Hey love! 💙 Check your messages — I just sent you the Prompt Studio link.

          
2 · Original DM — first time, carries the link
Hey love! 💙 You asked about the Prompt Studio — here it is: https://payhip.com/b/rLK92 It's the exact system I teach live, step by step, for $7. Grab yours and come tell me what you build with it! 🦋

          
3 · Nudge DM — returning person, new post
Hey love! 💙 Saw you on the new post — the Prompt Studio link is still right here when you're ready: https://payhip.com/b/rLK92 🦋

          
Now learn the voice rules that produced them:

          
    
            
  • Friendly, warm, casual, plain words. The way you talk to your people, because it is your people.
    • 
            
  • Emojis are welcome; stiff is not. If it reads like a company wrote it, it gets rewritten before it ever sends.
    • 
            
  • No em dashes in the messages — commas and short sentences carry the same warmth without the robot fingerprint.
    • 
            
  • The read-aloud test: say the message out loud. If you would not say it to a friend's face, it does not go out under your name.
    • 
            
  • Fixed copy, no improvising. The system sends these words and only these words. New wording is a decision you make on purpose, not a surprise the system invents.
    •

Why This Matters

          
“The scan can run itself. The sorting can run itself. The sending does not run itself until a human has looked at the batch and said the word. That pause is not a bug in the system — that pause IS the system.”

        

        

          
Follow Along

          
    
            
  1. Look at a finished scan batch: each match listed with who, which post, which pile (Original / Nudge / Skip), and the exact message that would go out. This is what lands in front of you for review.
    2. 
            
  2. Watch how review works: two get approved, one gets struck — a human edits the batch before anything sends. When it is your batch, you do the same. Only what survives your review sends.
    3. 
            
  3. Then learn the never-auto list. These are flagged for you, never answered by the system:
              
      
                
    • Refunds — money conversations are human conversations.
      • 
                
    • Access problems — “I paid and can't get in” gets a person, fast.
      • 
                
    • Upset buyers — nobody arguing with a template ever calmed down.
      • 
                
    • Anything the system is unsure about — if a reply needs a fact it cannot verify, it does not guess. It flags.
      • 
              
    
            
    4. 
          

          
Know the two modes. The default you start with is approval batches: nothing sends unreviewed. Later, on purpose and per offer, you may choose to let a proven kit send on its own once its batches have run clean — that is a promotion your system earns, never the starting point.

Troubleshooting — The Snags Card

          
“My automation does nothing at all.”
Nine times out of ten, the app is not connected in Muse. The automation can only touch what it is connected to. Go to Settings → Connectors, confirm the app shows connected, then run the scan again. This is the number one cause — check it first, always.

          
“Somebody got the link twice.”
A send happened without the log being checked or written. The fix is procedural, not technical: check before, write immediately after, every time. Then send that person nothing more — the next time they comment on a new post, they are a Nudge, not an apology tour.

          
“It matched comments that were not asking for anything.”
Your matching is too loose. The trigger must match as a whole word, case-insensitive — and if a match still looks wrong in the batch review, strike it at the approval gate. That gate exists for exactly this.

          
“My messages sound like a robot sent them.”
The copy drifted from your voice. Rewrite it plain and warm, keep the emojis you would actually use, take out the em dashes, and pass the read-aloud test before it goes back in the kit. Fixed copy only — the system never improvises its way back to human.

          
“It will not DM from my profile / my group.”
That is the surface working as designed, not a snag. Profiles have no true auto-DM, so matches get flagged for a manual reply; your own group gets public replies only. Full public-reply-plus-DM runs live on the Page and Instagram.

          
“A refund question got an auto-reply.”
It should not have — refunds, access problems, and upset buyers are on the never-auto list and get flagged for you. Check that the list is written into the kit, answer that person yourself right away, and do not let the next batch out until the flag rule is confirmed in the setup.

Your Seven Rules — Read Them Aloud

          
    
            
  1. Connect first. The automation can only touch what Muse is connected to — connectors confirmed connected before setup, every time.
    2. 
            
  2. Check the log before anything sends. Original once, a nudge on a new post, skip same-post repeats — nobody gets the same offer twice.
    3. 
            
  3. Approval before sending. A scan produces a draft batch; a human says send. Only what survives review goes out.
    4. 
            
  4. Lives get the link in the post. No trigger word on a live — everything else is trigger-word territory.
    5. 
            
  5. Free-code giveaways stay out of this system. One code, in the post, self-serve — trigger words are for paid offers and link requests.
    6. 
            
  6. Refunds, access problems, and upset people are flagged, never auto-answered. Money and feelings get a human.
    7. 
            
  7. Handles yes, passwords never. And no connector does not mean cannot be worked — it means the browser route.
    8. 
          

        

        

          
Follow Along

          
Read them slow, one at a time. After each one, think back to where you saw it happen in these lessons — the connector check, the three-way sort, the batch review. Rules you have watched happen are rules you will keep.

Your First Week — “Your First Approved Batch”

          
Within the next seven days: confirm every app your system touches shows connected in Muse, keep your kit on one offer, and run your scans on the rhythm you set — three a day. Review every batch before it sends, log every send the moment it goes out, and answer every flag yourself. At the end of the week, check your three numbers: matches found, sends logged, doubles sent — and that last number had better be zero.

        

        
You started this curriculum hoping you would notice the right comment at the right moment. You are finishing it with a system that watches on a schedule, remembers everybody it has ever answered, writes in your voice, and still waits for your word before it speaks for you. That system is now yours — set up for your offer, in your voice, under your control.

        
Keep this page bookmarked — your prompts, your log format, and your rulebook all live right here, ready every time you run a scan.

        
Now let your comments do the carrying.
